investigations.name: glucose-regulation
investigations.title: Act 1 · Model Trust — COPASI vs Tellurium
investigations.description: **Act 1 of 4** in the viva-human-atlas arc — **Trust → Atlas → Coverage → Connectivity**. The foundation: a cross-engine (COPASI vs Tellurium) correctness check on BioModels matching "glucose regulation", establishing a trustworthy fetch-and-compare spine. If two independent engines don't agree on the same model, nothing built on top of those models can be trusted — so this act earns that trust before Act 2 maps models onto HRA anatomy and Act 3 measures 3D coverage. → Next: **Act 2 · Atlas** (investigation `hra-integration`).
investigations.question:
For BioModels matching "glucose regulation", do COPASI and Tellurium agree on
the time-course dynamics — and which models diverge or fail to load in one engine?
investigations.hypothesis:
Most curated glucose-regulation SBML models integrate to near-identical
trajectories under COPASI and Tellurium; disagreements flag either engine-
specific loading issues or genuinely stiff/edge-case models worth follow-up.
Confirmed: a live 5-model run found the one curated `BIOMD*` model that
loaded in both engines (BIOMD0000000633, Bulik2016 hepatic glucose
metabolism) agrees near-perfectly (mean nRMSE 2.05e-07, "Good"),
cross-validated by the committed full-corpus dataset's independent
measurement of the same model (1.61e-07, also "good"). The other 4/5 —
all non-curated `MODEL*` preprint entries — failed identically on a
missing SED-ML file, an engine-agnostic loading gap rather than a
disagreement.

investigations.name: hra-3d
investigations.title: Act 3 · Coverage — Models on the HRA 3D Anatomy
investigations.description: **Act 3 of 4** in the viva-human-atlas arc — Trust → Atlas → **Coverage** → Connectivity. Consumes Act 2's organ→models atlas and asks the payoff question: *which of the HRA's anatomical structures actually have a mechanistic model, and where is the modeling white-space?* Builds the 3D-anatomy side of the fetch-and-compare spine: the full ASCT+B-3D crosswalk and a glomerulus FTU digital object, organ-granularity model coverage crossed with the biomodel-DO index at both query scale and full-corpus scale, model->AS->GLB-node spatial linkage, an end-to-end reproducible build pipeline (`atlas-pipeline`), a per-organ simulation pass (`kidney-model-simulation`), and a materialized three.js viewer pack. ← Prev: **Act 2 · Atlas** (`hra-integration`) · → Next: **Act 4 · Connectivity** (`model-connectivity`).
investigations.question:
Which of the HRA's 1,730 Uberon-keyed anatomical structures (2,295 raw
ASCT+B-3D crosswalk rows, 114 source-organ GLBs) are covered by a
mechanistic model — at a single query's scale and at the full
1,096-model curated-corpus scale — and can we view that coverage/linkage
directly on the 3D anatomy?
investigations.hypothesis:
The full ASCT+B-3D anatomical-structure crosswalk (2,295 rows, 1,730 with
a resolvable Uberon CURIE, below the ~81 per-organ reference-organ GLBs)
and a sub-organ-scale FTU digital object (glomerulus) are both loadable
via thin Steps; crossing the crosswalk with the hra-integration
investigation's biomodel-DO organ->models index (at organ granularity) is
enough to mark model coverage over anatomical structures/organs and to
join each covered model to the exact GLB scene node it maps to — giving a
coverage/linkage layer that a three.js viewer can render directly on a
reference-organ 3D model, without a heavyweight per-AS-node
model-matching pipeline. Confirmed: a single 25-result query covers only
58/1,730 AS nodes (liver + pancreas), while crossing the full curated
1,096-model corpus covers 635/1,730 (31/114 organs) — an order of
magnitude wider, and wide enough to newly reach kidney.

investigations.name: hra-integration
investigations.title: Act 2 · Atlas — Mapping Models to HRA Anatomy
investigations.description: **Act 2 of 4** in the viva-human-atlas arc — Trust → **Atlas** → Coverage → Connectivity. Takes the trustworthy models from Act 1 and gives each one an anatomical address. Builds the HRA (Human Reference Atlas) side of the fetch-and-compare spine, then closes the loop into the Atlas Browser: a thin CCF-API client (reference organs, cell-type terms, anatomical-structure terms); a biomodel Digital Object annotation layer with two complementary organ matchers — name-synonym matching over BioModels titles, and annotation-based matching over each model's own SBML MIRIAM/BTO metadata; a measured comparison of how much recall the annotation matcher adds over name-only matching; and the HRA Computational Model Atlas (`studies/hra-atlas-browser/viz/atlas/`) that renders the resulting organ->models index as an interactive 3D atlas a user can actually see biomodels attached to. ← Prev: **Act 1 · Model Trust** (`glucose-regulation`) · → Next: **Act 3 · Coverage** (`hra-3d`).
investigations.question:
Can we pull HRA datasets/knowledge via the live CCF API (reference organs,
cell-type terms, anatomical-structure terms) and link BioModels to HRA
anatomy (Uberon organs) via a transparent biomodel Digital Object +
organ->models index — and, having built that index, actually get the
resulting models onto the HRA atlas as something a user can see?
investigations.hypothesis:
The HRA CCF API's reference-organs, cell-type-term-occurences, and
ontology-term-occurences endpoints are stable enough to drive a Step-based
fetch inside a process-bigraph composite; and simple synonym matching over
BioModels names against the HRA reference-organ set is enough to annotate a
useful fraction of glucose-regulation models with an Uberon organ, giving a
working organ->models index without a heavyweight NLP classifier.
Confirmed: live runs loaded 81 reference organs (69/81 Uberon-keyed),
149 Cell Ontology terms, and 288 anatomical-structure terms; synonym
matching over 25 "glucose regulation" search hits tagged 5/25 (20%) with
an HRA organ — 4 pancreas, 1 liver — a real but recall-limited (name-only)
organ->models index, not a complete one.

investigations.name: model-connectivity
investigations.title: Act 4 · Connectivity — How the Curated Models Couple
investigations.description: **Act 4 of 4** in the viva-human-atlas arc — Trust → Atlas → Coverage → **Connectivity**. The integration layer: a model-to-model network over the curated corpus, with edges for shared molecular species (mechanistic coupling / variable coverage) and shared HRA anatomy (tissue co-location), plus an interactive force-graph explorer to navigate it. Answers "how do the models we curated connect?" directly.
investigations.question:
Having trusted the models (Act 1), given them an anatomical address (Act 2),
and measured their 3D coverage (Act 3): do the curated models actually form a
connected network through shared biological content — which variables do they
share, how densely do they couple, and is there a mechanistic backbone, or
just isolated islands?
investigations.hypothesis:
Two models are coupleable to the extent they share biological variables:
molecular species (CHEBI/UniProt/KEGG/GO/Reactome identifiers) for mechanistic
coupling, and HRA anatomy (organ/FTU/cell type) for tissue co-location. A
shared-variable network over the corpus should reveal a dominant connected
backbone centered on core-metabolism variables rather than a scatter of
disconnected models.
Confirmed: over the 2,554-model corpus, 1,456 models carry at least one
shareable variable; after dropping ubiquitous stop-word terms, the molecular
layer links them into a single dominant component of 634 models (43.5% of the
connected set) around hub variables ATP (CHEBI:15422, 83 models), translation
(GO:0006412, 119), and apoptosis (GO:0008219, 101) — a real, navigable
model-coupling network, not isolated islands.
